summary: SecVecCoder trains secure and vulnerable LoRA adapters with localized preference optimization (LPO) on 803 SVEN secure/vulnerable pairs, then adds the secure task vector and subtracts a scaled vulnerable task vector from the base weights. On CodeGuard+ (17 main-CWE scenarios, Python and C/C++) it raises sec-pass@1 (functional and CodeQL-clean) for six 1.3B-7B open coding models at essentially no decoding overhead.

claims.claim: Improves trustworthy completions (sec-pass@1) by 2.1-36.0 pp over base across six models
claims.evidence: Table V main-CWE sec-pass@1; 36.0 appears in the table body (line ~1588). n=100 samples per scenario at T=0.1 over 17 scenarios; no seeds/CIs on the accuracy numbers.

claims.claim: State-of-the-art on five of six models vs SVEN, SafeCoder, CoSec, SCoDE, DeepGuard
claims.evidence: §V-A2: exceeds strongest prior defense by 3.8-27.5% on five models; loses on DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B (68.2 vs SafeCoder 79.3). SafeCoder run with its original corpus/default configuration rather than retuned.

claims.claim: Generalizes to unseen CWEs (up to +39.1 pp)
claims.evidence: §V-A3: gains 2.0-39.1 pp over base on all six models; but SafeCoder beats it by 19.3-29.6 pp on both StarCoder2 models, which the authors attribute to SafeCoder having seen those CWEs. 'Unseen' set is small.

claims.claim: Decoding latency within 0.6% of base on average; 8.0-12.5% of SafeCoder training cost
claims.evidence: §V-B, Table VI, Fig. 5: five runs, 95% CIs within +/-3% (Qwen-3B within +/-5%); training 0.68-1.80 A6000 GPU-hours.
Table VII ablation: removing tau_sec costs 0.3-18.1 pp (avg 8.0), removing tau_insec costs 4.2-20.3 pp (avg 11.1).

patterns.note: Weight-space fine-tuning/task-vector steering improves joint functional+secure generation on small open models.
CodeQL is used only as the evaluation oracle, not as in-loop feedback.

methodology.sample: CodeGuard+ 17 main-CWE scenarios plus a small unseen-CWE set; 100 completions per scenario; 6 validation scenarios used for hyperparameter sweeps
methodology.baselines: SVEN, SafeCoder, CoSec, SCoDE, DeepGuard (current secure-codegen methods), plus SFT- and SafeCoder-derived task vectors
methodology.variance: Latency over 5 runs with 95% CIs; no seeds or CIs for sec-pass@1
methodology.ablations: Fine-tuning strategy, steering operator, steering strength, temperature, component removal
methodology.contamination_controls: Notes that 'unseen' CWEs are in some baselines' training data; no check of base-model pretraining contamination

biases.detail: 17 main scenarios; unseen-CWE set is a handful of scenarios.
No seed variation or CIs for the headline sec-pass@1 numbers.
Security judged solely by CodeQL queries per scenario; CodeQL false negatives count as 'secure'.
Short function-level completions (max 512 tokens) on small models, far from agentic repository work.

verdict_reason: off-topic for the harness KB: a sound weight-steering method for <=7B open coding models on function-level Python/C completions; it requires access to model weights and says nothing about agent harness design.
applicability: Does not transfer: the Java team uses hosted frontier models through agent hosts and cannot apply task vectors to their weights; evaluation is Python/C only and single-function. The only takeaway is methodological: measure security and functionality jointly (sec-pass) when gating agent output, e.g. require tests and a CodeQL/Semgrep pass together on ingestion code rather than reporting them separately.
